label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson) - Aria 3 recalibration

Last month Dana asked on the General board whether anyone had used Harbor Point, and I said I'd write it up once my machine had been through a real trial. It has now been through eight days of a civil trial, so here is the review.

THE BASICS

Equipment: Stenvale Aria 3
Work requested: full recalibration, number bar sensor inspection, cleaning, firmware update
Dropped off: Monday, October 19
Picked up: Tuesday, October 27 (6 business days; I was quoted 10)
Quoted: $285
Paid: $310. The extra $25 was a battery replacement I approved along the way.
Loaner: Yes, a Stenvale Aria 2
Who paid: Me. I buy all my own equipment, and there is no reimbursement from the court.

THE SHOP

Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road in Towson, with free parking in back. Gloria Ruark is the technician and the person I dealt with from start to finish.

THE WORK

The invoice lists a full keyboard recalibration, the number bar depression sensor replaced, an internal cleaning, firmware updated from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1, and the internal battery replaced. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

The battery is worth a note. Gloria emailed to say it was holding only about 60% of rated capacity, quoted $25 for the replacement, and told me she would not go ahead without my approval. I appreciated being asked, and I said yes. $310 is fair for what was done.

The machine also came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment made. In all my years of having machines serviced, nobody has given me that before.

HOW IT HELD UP

My first full day back on the Aria was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. It has now been through eight days of trial.

THE LOANER

The Aria 2 loaner was a real help, but its tilt arm would not hold position. It slipped in the middle of an afternoon deposition, and I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I told Gloria by email, and she said they would repair it. A small thing, but if you borrow it, check the arm before you take it out of the shop.

THE WEAKNESS

Phone hours are Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4, and that is all. If you work a Monday docket, or a Friday one, you cannot reach them by phone on those days. I called on Wednesday, October 21 to ask how things were going. It rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed me the next day, so I did get an answer, but it was not the answer I was calling for. Email is the way to reach them, so plan around that. If you need a quick answer during a hearing week, it will be frustrating.

BOTTOM LINE

Dana, to answer what you actually asked: yes, I would trust them with your Aria. The turnaround beat the estimate, the price matched the work, they asked before spending my money, and the paperwork was better than I have had anywhere. The loaner means you are not stuck without a machine while it is in the shop, which I know matters for you. The cost is that you will be working by email, and the tilt arm on the loaner was not up to the job.

If anyone else has been there, add your experience below.

Maureen Calloway
